attempts: All 4 get_test_case_detail probe calls returned HTTP 200 with data.success=true.
Each response was ~1.0-1.06MB, mostly from the undeclared `testcase_template` field (~1.05-1.14MB of that per response) - noted as an efficiency concern, not correctness.

item_shape.test_case_steps: array of step objects (id, step, order, title, result, ... ), never the declared single object
item_shape.steps: always [] even when test_case_steps is non-empty
item_shape.test_run_results_count: integer, but WRONG on verified data (see prod_vs_preprod below)

declared_missing: using_fallback_template - never appeared in any of the 4 probed responses despite being called out in guidance prose.
undeclared_returned: automation_state (full descriptor, distinct from the declared automation_status:{name,value})
estimated_duration_seconds (real value; declared `estimate` field is always null as guidance says)
reviewers (array, empty on all probed cases) and review_status (string, e.g. 'pending') - NOT called out in the preprod undeclared-field list; new additional undeclared fields observed on prod.

count_drift_check.threshold_hypothesis_note: Real per-case result count for BOTH cases, independently confirmed via two separate read capabilities (list_test_results_for_test_case_by_integer_id v1 AND v2), is exactly 1. get_test_case_detail reported test_run_results_count=2 for BOTH cases - the identical wrong number, and it exactly equals TR-4827350's combined total (1 Failed + 1 Passed = 2). This strongly suggests the counter is scoped to the wrong entity (the whole run, or some case-agnostic aggregate) rather than genuinely counting results for the specific test case - a SCOPE bug, not a volume-threshold bug: the drift appears already at N=1 real result, which argues against the preprod hypothesis that counts only break above some large N. A second data point (TC-1041803, id 38648438, in TR-3866741/folder 7772651) showed test_run_results_count=1 even though that same run's own case-grid (list_test_run_test_cases_by_integer_id) reports this exact case as never-executed ('untested'/'Untested') in that run, and list_test_results_for_test_case_by_integer_id confirmed 0 results for that case in that run - another instance of the count field disagreeing with the case's real per-run execution state, again in the OVER-count direction rather than preprod's zero-out direction.

prod_vs_preprod.test_case_steps_type: Declared as a single OBJECT in the schema; actual response is ALWAYS an ARRAY of step objects on prod too - confirmed non-empty (5, 5, 11 items on three different cases) and empty ([]) on a case with no steps (TC-838571). Exactly reproduces the preprod type-level drift.
prod_vs_preprod.steps_sibling_field: The sibling `steps` array (declared, distinct from test_case_steps) stayed [] on every probed case, INCLUDING the ones where test_case_steps carried 5-11 real step objects - reproduces the preprod finding that `steps` never actually gets populated.
prod_vs_preprod.summary: The preprod DRIFT reproduces on production, but the count-drift half reproduces as a DIFFERENT failure mode than what was seen on preprod, not an identical repro. On preprod, test_run_results_count/issues_count/issues read 0/0/[] for a case independently verified to have 14 real results (a zero-out/under-count). On prod, the same fields are also independently verifiable as WRONG - but they read a non-zero, INFLATED number (2) that matches the run's combined total rather than the individual case's real count (1) - on two separate cases in the same run, and a further disagreement (1 reported vs. 0 real-in-that-run) on a third case in a different run. So on both environments the count fields are untrustworthy against verified real data, but the direction/shape of the wrongness differs (preprod: floor-to-zero; prod: appears to leak the run/aggregate total into the per-case field), and prod shows the drift is present even at tiny result counts (N=1), which argues against a pure large-N threshold explanation. The test_case_steps type-level drift (object declared, array always returned) and the steps-stays-empty finding reproduce exactly and verbatim on production. field_name is present and populated on case_type/priority/status/automation_state, matching preprod.

notes: TR-3866741, as referenced in the fixture ('21 results total, 1 Blocked'), currently shows 0 executed results across all 16 of its listed test cases in production (all 'untested') - the fixture data for this run appears to have drifted/reset since it was recorded, independent of the capability under test; this was cross-checked with both list_test_run_test_cases_by_integer_id and list_test_results_for_test_case_by_integer_id before concluding it wasn't a probing error. Separately, get_test_run_progress 404'd on both the TR-3866741 identifier and its bare numeric run id, while list_test_run_test_cases_by_integer_id resolved the TR- identifier fine for the same run - a minor cross-capability inconsistency noted in passing, not part of this capability's contract. testcase_template bloats every response to ~1-1.1MB, which is an efficiency/token-cost concern worth flagging to the product team even though it's not a contract violation per se.
